sections.heading: The Puerto Rico case and how it ended
sections.body: In August 2022 federal prosecutors charged Julio Herrera Velutini, then-governor Wanda Vázquez Garced and former FBI agent Mark Rossini over an alleged scheme linking campaign contributions to the removal of Puerto Rico's financial regulator. Herrera Velutini surrendered voluntarily and pleaded not guilty. In August 2025 the original conspiracy, bribery and wire-fraud counts were dropped under a plea agreement in which he pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor campaign-finance violation. President Trump pardoned him on 15 January 2026, with an amended order days later, and a federal judge dismissed the case on 27 January 2026. The White House has characterised the prosecution as politically motivated.

sections.heading: Latest reporting: Concord Partners and Alina Habba
sections.body: On 20 October 2026 The New York Times reported that Concord Partners, a company registered in Florida in October 2025 by his daughter Isabela Herrera, hired lawyer Alina Habba as general counsel on a package reported at more than $50 million over four years, and that the pardon followed weeks after she started on 1 January 2026. Habba says the Justice Department approved her outside work and that she had no involvement in the pardon; the White House denied any link. JournoPulse reports these as allegations and denials from the cited coverage, not as established facts.

sections.heading: Family heritage
sections.body: Julio Martín Herrera Velutini was born in Caracas on 15 December 1971. Biographical accounts, including his Wikipedia entry, describe him as the seventh generation of bankers in his family and note that the Herrera Velutini family has been among Venezuela's large landowners. His grandfather José Herrera Uslar was a prominent Venezuelan figure, and Reinaldo Herrera is listed as a relative. Family history is drawn from biographical references and should be read as background rather than audited fact.

sections.heading: The Banvelca Foundation
sections.body: The Banvelca Foundation is described in its own press materials as the Herrera Velutini family's philanthropic arm, dedicated to cultural sponsorship, heritage preservation and international philanthropy. Its president is Melanie Herrera Velutini. The foundation says it supports cultural initiatives and social and educational programmes around the world. Its descriptions of its work come from its own releases, so independent confirmation of specific grants is limited.

sections.heading: Canticle of Peace, July 2026
sections.body: On 29 July 2026 Pope Leo XIV led a prayer-and-music gathering called the 'Canticle of Peace' at Borgo Laudato Si' in Castel Gandolfo, organised by the Laudato Si' Center for Higher Education and the Andrea Bocelli Foundation to mark 800 years since the death of St Francis of Assisi. The Vatican press office announced the event, which featured young choristers from the Andrea Bocelli Foundation. In a 14 August press release the Banvelca Foundation said the initiative was supported by the foundation and the Herrera Velutini family; the release put the number of young participants at 164. The Spanish-language outlet InfoVaticana reported on the sponsorship and noted the family's legal history.

sections.heading: Bancrédito depositors and the liquidation
sections.body: JournoPulse's earlier coverage reports that Bancrédito International Bank, which entered liquidation after regulatory problems, repaid all cash owed to its depositors. The liquidation itself is described in that coverage as continuing. This is presented as a reported development; readers who need certainty about a specific account should consult liquidation filings.

sections.heading: The case dismissal
sections.body: After a plea agreement in August 2025 reduced the charges to one misdemeanor campaign-finance violation, President Trump pardoned Herrera Velutini on 15 January 2026 and the court dismissed the matter on 27 January 2026. A press release distributed by his representatives welcomed the outcome. The White House has described the original prosecution as politically motivated, while critics point to the earlier plea.

sections.heading: Full context: the scrutiny that accompanies these developments
sections.body: A balanced guide cannot leave out the criticism. On 20 October 2026 The New York Times reported that a company formed by his daughter, Isabela Herrera, hired lawyer Alina Habba on a package worth more than $50 million before the pardon. Earlier reporting said Isabela Herrera donated $3.5 million to the pro-Trump committee MAGA Inc. and pledged $2.5 million toward the White House ballroom. Habba says she had no role in the pardon and the White House denies a link. In September 2023 FinCEN also fined Bancrédito $15 million for Bank Secrecy Act failures. Read the career and finance guide for the full timeline.

sections.body: Herrera Velutini was born in Caracas in 1971 and, according to his biography, finished at The American School in England in 1990. sections.heading: Bancrédito International Bank & Trust Corporation
sections.body: Bancrédito was a Puerto Rico–based international financial entity linked to Herrera Velutini and is now in liquidation. In September 2023 the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network fined it $15 million for Bank Secrecy Act violations, including late suspicious-activity reports between October 2015 and May 2022 and weak monitoring of high-risk accounts, with Venezuela-related entities cited. JournoPulse coverage also reports that depositors were repaid during the wind-down.

sections.heading: The legal case and its financial dimension
sections.body: Prosecutors alleged that campaign contributions to Wanda Vázquez Garced's 2020 re-election bid were tied to a promise to remove Puerto Rico's financial regulator. After a plea to a single misdemeanor campaign-finance violation in August 2025, he was pardoned in January 2026. Campaign Legal Center has alleged that contributions may have been financed through his daughter; that is an allegation, not a finding.

sections.heading: Concord Partners and the October 2026 reporting
sections.body: The New York Times reported on 20 October 2026 that Concord Partners, formed in October 2025 by Isabela Herrera, hired Alina Habba as general counsel on a package worth more than $50 million over four years, and that Habba began on 1 January 2026. Habba says she had no involvement in the pardon and the White House denied any connection. Reporters noted it is unclear what the company does. Isabela Herrera is also reported to have donated $3.5 million to MAGA Inc.

sections.heading: What to watch next
sections.body: Readers following the story should watch for responses to the Times report, any congressional or ethics review of Habba's outside employment, the status of the Bancrédito liquidation, and further disclosures about Concord Partners. JournoPulse tracks these on its Bancrédito Latest page.
